newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ford's Brazil unit predicts loss in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Brazil unit predicts loss in 1997.

text.p: The senior executive of Ford do Brasil said the company would continue to post a loss in 1997 despite increased sales of its Fiesta model and the launch of the new compact-sized Ka, financial daily Gazeta Mercantil reported.
"We will probably show losses once again," Ford do Brasil president Ivan Fonseca e Silva was quoted as saying.
Fonseca said the loss was caused by Ford's $2.5 billion four-year Brazilian investment plan and the company's difficulties in setting up the Fiesta assembly line.
Last month, Ford Motor Co shares fell sharply after the company said the second-half performance of its Brazilian unit would be "substantially worse" than the first half.

Although Ford has not given separate financial results for Brazil, it said its Latin American operations posted a loss of $129 million in the first semester of 1996. Brazil is the largest of Ford's Latin American operations.
Ford is Brazil's fourth largest car maker. In September it sold 20,190 vehicles in the domestic market.
